transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I guess I'm here because... well, I just can't stop focusing on my face. There's this rough, sunken-looking patch on it. 

Every time I look in the mirror, or if I see a photo of myself, it's all I can see. It makes one whole side of me look real old and just... beat-up. The thing is, my family and other people keep telling me they barely notice anything at all, but I know what I'm looking at, and I just can't stop seeing it.
Do you find yourself performing any specific actions, like constantly checking mirrors or trying to cover or fix this area, to deal with how it makes you feel?

Yeah, I do. Especially before I head out to work, or... well, like if I'm supposed to go over to my sister's for game night. I'll just stand in the bathroom and keep checking the mirror. I'll turn my face back and forth under the different lights to see how bad it is, and I catch myself rubbing at the spot a lot. 

If I think it looks too obvious, I'll pull my hat down real low to try and cover it up. Or sometimes... I just make up an excuse not to go out at all.
How much has this preoccupation with your face interfered with your ability to perform your job or maintain your relationships with your family and friends?

It's definitely getting in the way. Like with work... I've actually been late getting out the door for my construction jobs because I get stuck in front of the mirror. And when I am on site, I've started dodging any photos the crew takes. If someone pulls out a camera, I just walk the other way. 

As for my family, well... I've been skipping out on some of those game nights I mentioned. I just don't want people looking at my face, you know? So it's just easier to stay home.

When you are checking your reflection in the mirror, do you feel like you are doing it to reduce the anxiety caused by the spot, or is it more because you feel an internal urge to make sure it looks exactly 'right'?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I don't think it's about making it look 'right,' because... well, it never looks right to me. It's always just that same beat-up patch. 

I guess I just get so worked up thinking about how obvious it is to everyone else, that I just have to go look. I need to see how bad it's showing right in that moment. I don't know if you'd call that anxiety or an urge... I just know it bothers me so much that I can't settle down until I go check.
Have any doctors, dermatologists, or other professionals ever actually confirmed that there is a physical abnormality or skin condition on that part of your face?

No, they haven't. I've been to a couple doctors, and they all just say the same thing—that they barely notice anything, or that it's just normal aging. But... I mean, I'm the one looking at it. I can't stop seeing this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face. Every time I look in the mirror or see a photo, it's right there. It just makes that whole side of my face look old and beat-up, no matter what anyone else says.
